(Search snippet content — Hansard, Immigration and Asylum Bill debate, 13 July 2026)

Small boats / Channel crossings:
- January to June 2026: 11,884 migrants arrived crossing the English Channel — a 41% decrease on the 19,982 who arrived in the same period in 2025.
- A single small boat crossed the Channel on Friday carrying 128 people, the largest number to make a single vessel journey, surpassing the previous record of 125 people set in September 2025.

Government figures cited in Parliament:
- Arrests of people smugglers up 55% in the last year
- Organised immigration crime disrupted on 3,700 occasions, up 46%
- In partnership with French law enforcement, 46,000 attempted Channel crossings stopped
- In May, nearly two-thirds of attempted small boat crossings were thwarted

Politics: Ahead of the Immigration and Asylum Bill returning to the Commons for second reading, Burnham faced pressure from almost 80 backbench Labour MPs who signed a private letter urging him to walk back Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood's reforms. Burnham voted in favour of the Bill at Second Reading in July 2026.
